text: The five signature-request operations are served by rwb-document on base /api/recovery/document/v1 with the legacy section 12 shapes rebased per DP-13 - create on /cases/{caseId}/signature-requests, list on the same path, read one on /signature-requests/{requestId}, read by external reference on /signature-requests with a query, and update on PATCH /signature-requests/{requestId} - while no API ID, query name, element name or response field of them is treated as settled: each is marked as not specified in the source documents and faked until the API Specification carries it.
why: signature_request is P5's by the ownership ruling, so the operations have to live here, but TSD P5 Appendix T-A.1 holds seventeen document operations and no signature path, the FSD P5 has no e-signature section, and the legacy key is a P6 story; the story therefore cannot copy a path or an ID from a source.
read: TSD P5 Document hub v2 T-A.1 and T2; FSD P5 Document hub v3; context pack Ownership rows; legacy RWB-E2-018 sections 1, 12 and 13; Template and Rules v1 R4 (naming) and DP-13.
confirm: Solution architect with the API Specification owner and the rwb-comms contract owner
impact: The API Specification, the service contract catalogue and the five operations rwb-comms calls; the paths change once at the API review and the caller's fake changes with them.

text: signature_request is a table of rwb_document and is created by this story from the legacy field list DF-DOC-096 to DF-DOC-107, with a unique index on external_ref, an index on (treatment_id, status), an index on (case_id, created_at desc) and a check constraint on method, on status and on a SIGNED row carrying signed_document_id; rwb-comms holds no copy of the table and reads the request only through the operations of this story.
why: The table is listed in the ownership rows of the P5 context pack and in the Architecture v5 catalogue while only TSD P6 T3.1 defines it, and the ownership ruling is the authority for which service holds a table; without a decision the table would be built twice or nowhere.
read: Context pack Ownership rows (12 tables); TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1; TSD P5 Document hub v2 T3.1; Architecture v5 slides 16 and 41; legacy RWB-E2-018 sections 11 and 13.
confirm: Data steward and the owners of rwb-document and rwb-comms
impact: One table in one schema, one migration, one set of constraints; TSD P6 loses the object at its next version and TSD P5 and the physical schema gain it.

text: The five platform contracts the applied patterns add (RWB-PLT-E1043-CON for DP-07, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON for DP-09, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON for DP-10, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON for DP-15, RWB-PLT-N001-CON for DP-19) and the rwb-case reference-data contract RWB-P3-E1043-CON are delivered by the wave-0 platform release train and by the rwb-case contract story before the wave-2 build of this story, and are therefore prerequisites of the build rather than rows of its dependency lists, which stay empty exactly as the Work Package fixes them.
why: The nine patterns of the story name one platform CON each in the DP table while the Work Package gives the story four empty lists; adding them as lane dependencies would deepen lane L-P5-W and contradict the plan the assembler merges.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 and R5.7 rule 8; Work Package B2-P5-006 story line; Architecture v5 slides 20 and 43.
confirm: Release manager and the platform library owners
impact: The dependency map, the build order of wave 2 and the lane depth; no story behaviour changes and the fakes carry the build until the libraries publish.

text: This story publishes one event and no signature event: the version add of the signed copy writes DocumentStored to the outbox in the same transaction and the event leaves on rwb.document.events.v1 as rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1 with the document ID, the case ID, the type code, the doc version, the write-once flag and the stored-at time only, while the signature request state is read by its callers through the five operations and never through a topic.
why: The catalogue of the service names two events only and no source gives a signature event a name, a payload or a consumer, so publishing one would invent a contract that no consumer can subscribe to.
read: TSD P5 Document hub v2 T5.3; context pack Events (EV-16 and EV-17); Architecture v5 slide 42; legacy RWB-E2-018 sections 4 and 12.
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-reporting owner
impact: The event catalogue and the AsyncAPI document of rwb.document.events.v1; a future signature fact is a new story with DP-09.

text: The signed PDF is written only through API-P5-005 as the next version of the agreement with write_once true, and the container, the WORM tier, the object size limit and the byte transfer of that call are held as configuration and as a container stub of the contract fakes, with the write-once flag and the version chain treated as the guarantee the story can test; no direct object-store write is made by this story and no boundary value is a constant.
why: The sources fix the requirement (write-once for legal types, about 2.8 TB by 2031) and the container family but no container, tier, size limit, transfer path or refusal shape, and the retention periods are open.
read: TSD P5 Document hub v2 T-A.2 (API-P5-005) and T7 (NFR-029, NFR-069); Architecture v5 slide 8; legacy RWB-E2-018 sections 4, 12 and 13.
confirm: SCB IT infrastructure with the rwb-document store owner
impact: The storage design behind API-P5-005 and the configuration of the feature switch; the story behaviour and the tests hold when the values are settled.

text: A result that arrives for a request already SIGNED, DECLINED or EXPIRED is refused with 409 and the legacy MSG-P3-005 kept word for word, and the five request operations declare the Documents right of TSD P5 T6.1 - C on the create, R on the three reads and U on the update and on the version add - with the scope applied and the refusal proved with RW-PHONECOL, which holds Documents R only.
why: The legacy story reused a rwb-case message for a closed request and named Treatment and offer rights that belong to another service's area, while the rwb-document matrix declares the Documents column only; a build cannot start without a refusal and a right per operation.
read: legacy RWB-E2-018 sections 12, 14 and 16; TSD P5 Document hub v2 T6.1 and T-A.1; TSD P6 Communications v2 T6.1.
confirm: Solution architect with the access owner and the message standard owner
impact: The RBAC matrix of rwb-document, the message standard and the access test of the five operations; a message of the owning service is owed at the next version.
